articles.body: All outputs are real tool calls to the Equibles MCP server from 21 October 2026, trimmed. Every congressional trading tracker shows the same table: who bought what. The table is the easy part. The hard part is reading it: when the trade happened versus when it was disclosed, how much money a "$1,001 to $15,000" row really is, and whether a row is stock at all. Here is how I ask an AI agent those questions, and the checks I run on its answers. Connect it first In Claude, open Customize → Connectors → Discover , search for Equibles, click Connect to Claude and Authorize . Then switch it on in a chat from + → Connectors . In ChatGPT it's Plugins , search Equibles, Install plugin . In Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http equibles https://mcp.equibles.com/mcp then /mcp to sign in.

articles.title: Separate Dialogue, Music, and Sound Effects in ComfyUI
articles.excerpt: A video arrives with one mixed soundtrack. You want to replace the dialogue, but keep the background music and sound effects. Muting the audio removes all three. I built ComfyUI-DBS to bring that sepa…
articles.body: A video arrives with one mixed soundtrack. You want to replace the dialogue, but keep the background music and sound effects. Muting the audio removes all three. I built ComfyUI-DBS to bring that separation into a ComfyUI workflow. It splits a soundtrack into music, sound effects, and speech , then lets you save the parts or combine them again. The repository includes a workflow that writes a new video using the music and effects, with the extracted dialogue saved separately. It runs locally on a CPU or NVIDIA CUDA GPU. The two available models total about 23 MB to download. This is an unofficial integration of Dynamic Band Splitting (DBS) , by Bingzhe Zhang, Kai Li, and Xiaolin Hu.

articles.body: Short answer: choose retrieval by the freshness window the claims answer promises, the control needed over changed and deleted records, and the citation evidence an adjuster must see; durable policy context and live claim context often belong on two paths. The alert arrives first. An adjuster sees a claim summary citing a coverage clause that was replaced this morning, while the intake queue is otherwise healthy. The symptom is not an exotic model failure. It is a retrieval contract that never said how fresh “current policy” had to be. This is a capacity-planning problem as much as a search problem. A claims intake bot has to answer quickly, but a fast answer built from stale exclusions is worse than a slower answer that admits it needs review.

articles.body: Finnish Counter-Strike 2 pro Aleksi “Aleksib” Virolainen is facing a possible four-month suspended prison sentence over alleged “aggravated tax fraud” after failing to declare income from in-game sticker sales. In Counter-Strike 2 , players can purchase virtual stickers and place them on their weapons. They are an in-game item that can be bought on the Steam Marketplace, the CS2 Store, or in capsules, as well as through third-party websites. It’s not uncommon for professional teams to get a cut of the money earned from sticker sales and other in-game purchases when they compete at major tournaments — and it’s this revenue that prosecutors say Virolainen failed to include on his tax forms.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program. After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars , the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind. The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon , but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems. Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth.
